Q: What does Flink SQL Lateral Table grammar mean A:

LATERAL JOIN in flink can be used to join with either table function or a subquery, which is slightly more readable than writing a JOIN or LEFT JOIN with an ON TRUE join condition.

Is it SQL standard to use LATERAL as the key word to express joining with table function or It is Flink that chooses LATERAL to express joining with table function

As of 2026, LATERAL JOIN is SQL industry standard for subqueries (MySQL) and postgreSQL (both subqueries and table functions)

postgreSQL lateral join over table function (from docs):

SELECT p1.id, p2.id, v1, v2
FROM polygons p1 CROSS JOIN LATERAL vertices(p1.poly) v1,
     polygons p2 CROSS JOIN LATERAL vertices(p2.poly) v2
WHERE (v1 <-> v2) < 10 AND p1.id != p2.id;

Snowflake SQL also supports LATERAL, but to express correlated subqueries.

Q: Should a C++ logger write method be defined as const? A:

Read Effective C++ Item 3 "Use const whenever possible" to understand the concept of logical constness vs bitwise constness, and you will understand when to use const and mutable. (Notice that the suggestion in this item that recommends adding const to function's return type is generally considered unnecessary and outdated.)

To answer your question directly: It depends on what the observable state of a Logger object is. A member function that does not modify the observable state of the object, i.e., keeps the object "look unmodified" during calls, should be declared const. That is the concept of "logical constness".
